# Warehouse Cycle Counting

Cycle counting is a continuous inventory management process in which a warehouse counts a small, predetermined subset of its stock on a regular schedule rather than conducting a full physical inventory once or twice a year. The goal is to maintain accurate inventory records year-round without halting warehouse operations.

## How It Works

The process begins with classifying inventory using an ABC analysis. **A-items** are high-value or high-velocity SKUs that represent a large portion of total inventory value, **B-items** are moderate, and **C-items** are low-value or slow-moving. Each class is assigned a different counting frequency. A-items might be counted monthly or weekly, B-items quarterly, and C-items semi-annually or annually. This ensures that the most critical items receive the most attention.

Once the schedule is set, warehouse staff or automated systems pull a daily or weekly list of SKUs to count. The count team physically locates each item, verifies the quantity on hand, and records the result—either on a paper form, a handheld RF scanner, or a mobile device connected to the warehouse management system (WMS).

## Reconciliation and Correction

After the count is recorded, the system compares the counted quantity against the perpetual inventory record. Any discrepancy is flagged as a variance. The team then investigates the cause, which may include receiving errors, data entry mistakes, mispicks, shrinkage, or system issues. Once the root cause is identified, the inventory record is adjusted to reflect the actual count, and a corrective action is documented to prevent recurrence.

## Benefits

Cycle counting eliminates the need for a disruptive full inventory freeze, improves data accuracy over time, surfaces process weaknesses early, and provides management with ongoing visibility into inventory health. When executed consistently, it can reduce inventory discrepancies by 80–90% compared to annual counting alone.

# Warehouse Cycle Counting

Cycle counting is a continuous inventory management process in which a warehouse counts a small, predetermined subset of its stock on a regular schedule rather than conducting a full physical inventory once or twice a year. The goal is to maintain accurate inventory records year-round without halting warehouse operations.

## How It Works

The process begins with classifying inventory using an ABC analysis. **A-items** are high-value or high-velocity SKUs that represent a large portion of total inventory value, **B-items** are moderate, and **C-items** are low-value or slow-moving. Each class is assigned a different counting frequency. A-items might be counted monthly or weekly, B-items quarterly, and C-items semi-annually or annually. This ensures that the most critical items receive the most attention.

Once the schedule is set, warehouse staff or automated systems pull a daily or weekly list of SKUs to count. The count team physically locates each item, verifies the quantity on hand, and records the result—either on a paper form, a handheld RF scanner, or a mobile device connected to the warehouse management system (WMS).

## Reconciliation and Correction

After the count is recorded, the system compares the counted quantity against the perpetual inventory record. Any discrepancy is flagged as a variance. The team then investigates the cause, which may include receiving errors, data entry mistakes, mispicks, shrinkage, or system issues. Once the root cause is identified, the inventory record is adjusted to reflect the actual count, and a corrective action is documented to prevent recurrence.

## Benefits

Cycle counting eliminates the need for a disruptive full inventory freeze, improves data accuracy over time, surfaces process weaknesses early, and provides management with ongoing visibility into inventory health. When executed consistently, it can reduce inventory discrepancies by 80–90% compared to annual counting alone.
